standard-dialogue-first-time.npc: Good day! What can I do for you?

standard-dialogue-first-time.player: Junior Jim told me that you might be able to help me out with sea charting.

standard-dialogue-first-time.npc: Ah, that I can do indeed. You see, I am a map maker extraordinaire.

standard-dialogue-first-time.player: I find that a little hard to believe...

standard-dialogue-first-time.npc: Don't let this fool you. It takes more than eyes to make a map. They named the mapping book after me, you see...

standard-dialogue-first-time.text: He flashes a copy of a book at you titled 'McAtless's Multitude of Maps'.
He shows you another called 'The Charlespendium of Sea Charts'.

standard-dialogue-first-time.npc: So, as you can now see, I am very much the man to speak to about this sort of thing.

standard-dialogue-first-time.text: If the player does not have a spyglass in their inventory:

steps.npc: Here, I have a spare spyglass you can have.

steps.text: Charles thrusts a spyglass into your hands.

steps.npc: You are quite welcome to use it to admire me from afar!

standard-dialogue-first-time.npc: So, what specifically would you like to know about charting?

options.text: How do I go about charting the sea?
Can you tell me more about a specific type of charting?
What do I get from charting the sea?
Can you tell me about your parrot?
How do I go about charting the sea?

steps.player: How do I go about charting the sea?

steps.npc: Well, that very much depends. You see, when it comes to charting, there are quite a few different things you'll want to track. What you need to do is going to vary depending on what it is you're tracking.
That said, the starting point is always going to be your captain's log. I actually helped author the standard log that we give out around the Pandemonium.
I made sure to include some big hints in there about the things you might find on your sailing adventures.

steps.text: You get the distinct impression you were just winked at by a blindfolded eye.

steps.player: You say there are a few different things I might want to track. What are they?

steps.npc: Well, you have both big and small points of interest, water currents, sea depths, weather patterns, and then there's also drink crates. They're a curious one that Steve likes people to track.

options.text: Can you tell me about charting smaller points of interest?

steps.player: Can you tell me about charting smaller points of interest?

steps.npc: Well, you'll likely spot some interesting things in the sea and on some of the less explored islands that you find whilst out sailing.
Charting these things is simple. All you need to do is just make a note of them as you find them!

steps.text: Many points of interest don't require any tools to chart. Just interact with them from your boat or while on foot when close enough to them.

options.text: Can you tell me about charting larger points of interest?

steps.player: Can you tell me about charting larger points of interest?

steps.npc: Ah, for them, you'll want to find a good spot and use a spyglass to take it all in.

steps.player: But how do I know where a good spot is?

steps.npc: That can take a bit of practice, but if you pay close attention, you might find some very subtle, definitely not obvious signs of where the best places are...

steps.text: The spyglass can be used to chart larger points of interest. You can do so either from your boat or while on foot. Keep an eye out for the sparkly white circles that show where a spyglass can be used.

options.text: Can you tell me about drink crates?

steps.player: Can you tell me about drink crates?

steps.text: If the player has not completed Prying Times:

steps.npc: They're a bit of an interesting one. It's been argued that they're not actually completely essential for charting the sea, but Steve thinks otherwise. Probably best you talk to him if you want to know more.

steps.text: You need to complete the Prying Times quest to learn about drink crates.
If the player has completed Prying Times:

steps.npc: They're a bit of an interesting one. On your travels, you may spot some sealed crates floating in the sea.
Once you find one, just pry it open with your crowbar. If you're lucky, there will be a refreshing beverage inside for you to try.
Be careful though, as some of them can be a tinge on the ripe side...

steps.player: I must admit, I'm not totally sure what these crates have to do with charting...

steps.npc: Yes, that opinion has come up before. However, according to Steve, it's an unwritten rule in this world that alcohol is the key to solving all problems.
It's also been said that these crates add a bit of much needed danger to the whole charting effort.

steps.player: I see...

steps.text: Floating crates of drink can be found at sea and pried open with a crowbar. Once open, you can sample what you find inside. However, take care, for expired alcohol can be dangerous...

options.text: Can you tell me about tracking currents?

steps.player: Can you tell me about tracking currents?

steps.npc: Absolutely! Understanding the various currents around the seas is essential. As you sail around, you'll likely spot many currents of potential interest.

steps.text: If the player has not completed Current Affairs:

steps.player: But once I spot them, how do I track them?

steps.npc: Ah, for that, you'll need the right tool. Well, I suppose in this case, it's less of a tool and more of a friend.

steps.player: What do you mean?

steps.npc: It will probably make more sense if you head out and discover the art of tracking currents for yourself!
We had someone passing through recently who said that Arhein in Catherby was looking to track some currents. I'd suggest you go and speak to him.

steps.text: You need to complete the Current Affairs quest to learn about tracking currents.
If the player has completed Current Affairs:

steps.npc: To track them, you'll need to make use of your good friend, the current duck! Specifically, once you've found some currents you want to track, you'll want to let your current duck head out for a swim.
He'll track the currents for you, so all you need to do is follow him wherever he goes. Once he's done, just pick him up again and let him share what he discovered with you.

steps.player: Is this really the standard way of doing this?

steps.npc: Of course! I simply can't think of any alternatives!

steps.text: A current duck can be used to track currents. To do so, find an area of circularly expanding currents and release your duck there. Then just follow the duck with your boat and collect it again once it stops.

options.text: Can you tell me about checking sea depths?

steps.player: Can you tell me about checking sea depths?

steps.text: If the player does not have 38 Sailing:

steps.npc: Ah, for that, you'll need to go diving. However, you don't want to rush it. You'll need to make sure you're skilled enough for that sort of thing before you... dive in.

steps.text: You require 38 Sailing to learn about checking sea depths.
If the player does has 38 Sailing:

steps.npc: Ah, for that, you'll need to go diving. Doing so will let you take a record of the sea depth, but it's also great for learning more about the local underwater flora and fauna.
However, I wouldn't reccomend going it alone. Fortunately, a lot of mermaids have been popping up recently, interested in the extra sea traffic.
I hear they will guide you for a price, and for some inexplicable reason, that price seems to be solving a word-based puzzle for them.

steps.player: A puzzle?

steps.npc: Indeed, so get your thinking cap on... under your diving gear of course. It's very important you don't forget that.

steps.text: To check sea depths, you'll need to find a mermaid in the ocean, don some diving gear and then answer her puzzle. She'll then guide you down to the bottom of the sea for you to document your findings.

options.text: Can you tell me about tracking weather patterns?

steps.player: Can you tell me about tracking weather patterns?

steps.text: If the player does not have 57 Sailing:

steps.npc: Well, all good captains need to have a strong understanding of the weather out at sea. However, it requires a fair bit of skill to do it well. I'd suggest you wait until you're more experienced.

steps.text: You require 57 Sailing to learn about tracking weather patterns.
If the player has 57 Sailing:

steps.npc: Of course! All good captains need to have a strong understanding of the weather out at sea. However, to do it well, you'll probably want to enlist the help of a meteorologist.

steps.player: Where can I find one of those?

steps.npc: Well, it's a bit of an odd one, but I've been told there's a troll who has started working as one recently.

steps.player: A troll?

steps.npc: Indeed. It's a bit unusual, but who am I to judge! Anyway, apparently she's aquired a portable weather station, a very fine piece of equipment for measuring weather data.
If you come across this troll, she'll hopefully allow you to use this weather station for yourself.

steps.player: And how is it used?

steps.npc: Well, what you'll find is that the wind typically blows in large circles. What you need to do is find the middle of this circle, or the eye as we often call it.

You can use the weather station to work out the wind direction. If you follow it for a bit, you should be able to work out which way the circle is curving, and from that, you should be able to find the eye.
Just remember not to keep following the wind forever, or you'll just keep going around in circles!
Anyway, once you reach the eye, you can use the weather station to take the readings you need. After that, just make sure to return the weather station to the troll.

steps.text: To track weather patterns, you'll need to find the troll meteorologist, take her portable weather station and use it to find the eye of a circular wind storm. Once there, you can use the weather station to record your data.

steps.player: Let's talk about something else.

steps.npc: Very well.

options.text: What do I get from charting the sea?

steps.player: What do I get from charting the sea?

steps.npc: Other than the thrill of exploration?

steps.player: Yes, other than that.

steps.npc: Well, the more you know about the sea, the more you'll be able to take advantage of it. Specifically, learning about the seas will offer the discerning captain a shortcut or two.
And for the less discerning captain, I have a stock of alcohol I'd be willing to part with for up to date charting information, along with some coins of course.
My observational skills are not what they used to be after all!

steps.text: You get the distinct impression you were just winked at by a blindfolded eye.

steps.npc: Finally, in return for charting information, I can offer some training that will help you improve your sailing abilities. Just let me know any time you completely chart an ocean.

options.text: Can you offer me some training?

steps.player: Can you offer me some training?

steps.text: Charles takes your charts and shows them to his parrot.
If the player has no bonus XP to claim:

steps.npc: Sorry, but it doesn't look like you have anything in here that I don't already know.

steps.text: The parrot glares at you.
If the player has bonus XP to claim, but is not at the required level to claim it:

steps.npc: Yes, it looks like I can...
Oh, on second thoughts, it doesn't look like you have anything in here that I don't already know.

steps.text: If the player has bonus XP to claim:

steps.npc: Yes, it looks like I can...

steps.text: Charles gives a long-winded lecture on luffing.
Charles deep dives into the known history of mermaids.
Charles gives a refresher on the safe consumption of alcohol (through mouthfuls of grog).
Charles stops you in your tracks with his heavy analysis of anchor usage.
Charles tells you a tall tale about mast management.
Charles spots you through some spyglass handling training.
Charles builds your confidence with a well constructed lesson on ship repairs.

options.text: Can you tell me about these shortcuts?

steps.player: Can you tell me about these shortcuts?

steps.npc: Absolutely! As you become more familiar with the sea, you will likely start to notice rapid flowing waters where you hadn't before.
Assuming you have a strong enough helm on your boat, sailing over them should give you a noticable speed boost!

options.text: Can you tell me about these drinks?

steps.player: Can you tell me about these drinks?

steps.npc: Of course! There's the kraken ink stout, the perildance bitter, the trawler's trust, and of course, the horizon's lure! Which do you want to hear more about?

steps.player: Kraken ink stout.

steps.npc: Well, kraken ink stout is the perfect drink if you consider yourself a bit of a magical sailor as it's said to improve both your sailing and magical abilities.
Many claim that it also increases the likelihood of encountering interesting things while out at sea. I'm not sure how a drink does that, but the world works in strange ways.

steps.text: Having a keg of kraken ink stout on your boat will improve the chance of random encounters spawning at sea by 4%.
If the player hasn't completely charted 5 seas in the Ardent Ocean and 5 seas in the Unquiet Ocean:

steps.npc: While I'd love to sell you some, I'm afraid you need to do some more charting first.

steps.text: Buying kraken ink stout requires the following: Completely chart five seas in the Ardent Ocean. Completely chart five seas in the Unquiet Ocean.
If the player has completely charted 5 seas in the Ardent Ocean and 5 seas in the Unquiet Ocean:

steps.npc: Anyway, I'm pleased to say that you've done enough charting for me to sell you some! Would you like to buy a glass to sample it? Or do you want enough to fill a keg?

steps.prompt: Buy 1 x kraken ink stout for 300 coins?

steps.text: If the player does not have enough space or money:

steps.npc: Even I can see you don't have space to hold that, and just to be completely clear, I am totally blind!

steps.text: If the player has enough space and money:
Charles sells you 1 x kraken ink stout.

steps.npc: There you go! Enjoy! Now, are you interested in any other drinks?

steps.player: Actually, I'll pass.

steps.npc: Very well. Would you like me to tell you about a different drink?

steps.npc: Ah, they say perildance bitter is the best drink you'll find for a sailor who likes to get themselves into a fight or two. It will supposedly improve your strength, along with your sailing and ranging abilities.
But that's not all, for plenty of sailors also claim that a bit of perildance bitter has helped them out of a tight spot by improving their ability to man their boat cannons.

steps.text: Having a keg of perildance bitter on your boat will increase the max hit of your cannons by one.
If the player has not charted 8 seas in the Western Ocean and 5 seas in the Shrouded Ocean:

steps.npc: While I'd love to sell you some, I'm afraid you need to do some more charting first.

steps.player: Trawler's trust.

steps.npc: Well, as the name suggests, trawler's trust is the drink you want if you're planning to head out trawling. It's said to improve both your sailing and fishing abilities.
I've been told before that drinking it also helps you catch more fish when out deep sea trawling.

steps.text: Having a keg of trawler's trust on your boat will give a 5% chance to catch an extra fish whilst deep sea trawling.
If the player hasn't completely charted 50 seas:

steps.npc: While I'd love to sell you some, I'm afraid you need to do some more charting first.

steps.player: Horizon's lure.

steps.npc: Ah, the old classic. In many ways, there's nothing too fancy about horizon's lure. It's quite simply the perfect drink when all you care about is sailing.
Not only is it said to make you a better sailor, but it apparently also helps you improve your sailing abilities faster.

steps.text: Having a keg of horizon's lure on your boat will give a 2.5% boost to all Sailing experience gained.

steps.player: Can you tell me about your parrot?

steps.text: The previously still parrot turns its head to look you in the eye.

steps.npc: That's Spot. He's my seeing eye parrot. Say hello, Spot!

steps.text: The parrot reluctantly bows its head slightly.

steps.player: Not very talkative is he?

steps.text: Spot narrows his eyes at you.

steps.npc: Afraid he's mute. He hasn't talked for a good long time, but he still finds ways to express himself.
